- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Lexical semantics is the branch of linguistics concerned with the meaning of words and their combinations.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The study of lexical semantics has a rich and diverse history, with contributions from many prominent figures across different eras.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Aristotle's "Categories" presented a classification system for words based on their meaning, dividing words into categories such as substance, quality, and relation.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Peter Abelard developed a theory of word meaning that emphasized the relationship between words and their referents in the 12th century CE.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Thomas Aquinas extended Abelard's work in the 13th century CE, arguing that words could be divided into categories based on their meaning.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] John Wilkins published "An Essay Towards a Real Character and a Philosophical Language" in 1653, proposing a classification system for words based on their semantic features.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] John Locke's "Essay Concerning Human Understanding" in 1686 argued that words are signs that stand for ideas in the mind.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Port-Royal Grammar was published in 1765, proposing a classification system for words based on their semantic features.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Immanuel Kant's "Critique of Pure Reason" in 1781 developed a theory of meaning based on the relationship between words and concepts.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] August Schleicher proposed the "Stammbaumtheorie" in 1854, positing that languages develop from a common ancestral language.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Wilhelm Wundt published "Elements of Folk Psychology" in 1879, arguing that language is a product of social interaction.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Leonard Bloomfield's "Introduction to the Study of Language" in 1916 presented a theory of meaning based on the distribution of words in a sentence.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Ferdinand de Saussure's "Course in General Linguistics" was published in 1918, laying the foundations for structural linguistics.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Charles Ogden and Ivor Richards published "The Meaning of Meaning" in 1923, proposing a theory of meaning based on the relationship between words and their referents.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Gottlob Frege's "Begriffsschrift" was published in 1933, developing a theory of meaning based on the distinction between sense and reference.
